content:
{
  "claim": "recover_json_object ignores duplicate-key candidates inside code fences, so it can score a later top-level object outside the fence instead of the last fenced object, contrary to the documented rule that the last object inside a code fence is scored when any fence holds one.",
  "expected": "For content with a fenced JSON object containing repeated keys followed by a top-level object outside the fence, recover_json_object should return the fenced object with the repeated key resolved last-wins (e.g. {'b': 2}).",
  "observed": "It returns the later top-level object outside the fence (e.g. {'a': 1}) because the fenced candidate is skipped in the fenced pool (duplicate keys are only resolved for top-level candidates) and the top-level pool then selects the later object.",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"b\":1, \"b\":2}\n```\n{\"a\":1}",
  "source_basis": "recover_json_object doc: \"The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text\" and \"A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable\".",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Any reply containing a fenced JSON object with duplicate keys and a later top-level object outside the fence that parses as strict JSON.",
  "uncertainty": "The doc could be read as making fenced candidates strict-only, but the general 'candidate' sentence and the last-fence rule make the intended behaviour clear."
}
